text:
A: Hey! Oh, there you are. Can you hear me alright?
B: Yes, hi, I can hear you. Sorry, my camera was frozen for a second.
A: No worries, mine does that constantly. I'm Jago, by the way.
B: Tereza. Nice to meet you.
A: Tereza, lovely. Did you do that puzzle bit at the start? I was proper rubbish at it, I just kept dragging things around hoping.
B: Oh, the puzzle, yes. I think I did okay? I was very slow though, I like to check everything twice, so, erm... yeah. [laughs]
A: See, that's the sensible way. So where are you calling from?
B: East London, Leyton. I'm originally from Czech Republic, from Brno, but I'm here eight years now.
A: Oh nice. I'm the opposite end of the country, Truro in Cornwall. Born and bred, never escaped. What do you do up there?
B: I'm a clinical trials coordinator, at a hospital. So I schedule patients for their visits, I keep all the paperwork ready for audits, I process blood samples for the courier. It sounds boring, I know, but I quite like it. Somebody has to notice the missing signature, you know?
A: No, that's not boring, that's important. Honestly, I need someone like you in my life. I'm doing a film degree, final year, and I'm making a documentary about gig rowing, the old Cornish rowing boats, and the logistics side of it is just, like, chaos. Call sheets everywhere, tide times, I keep forgetting release forms.
B: Release forms! That is exactly my job, consent forms. You must get them signed before, not after.
A: Yeah, I've learned that the hard way. [laughs] But the filming bit's proper good. I'm out on the water at six in the morning with these clubs, some of the rowers are in their seventies and they just tell you everything once the camera's on.
B: That sounds lovely, actually. Six in the morning on the sea, though. Is it cold?
A: Freezing. I got soaked twice last week. Worth it though. I've sent it off to a couple of festivals, so fingers crossed, do you know what I mean?
B: Oh wow, good luck. I would be too nervous to send something like that.
A: Oh, I'm bricking it, to be fair. Do you get back to Brno much?
B: Twice a year, yes. I fly, but I'm terrible flyer, I hold the armrest like this the whole take-off. My husband laughs at me.
A: Ha. Have you done much travelling round Europe then? I interrailed for five weeks when I was twenty. Lisbon was my favourite, hands down.
B: We went to Porto, me and Tom, for a long weekend. It was beautiful. The bridge, and the custard tarts, I ate maybe ten.
A: Only ten? Rookie numbers. No, Porto's meant to be unreal. I keep saying I'll go back to Portugal, and then Japan after I graduate, it's basically booked.
B: Basically booked, or booked?
A: [laughs] Okay, it's in my head. That's basically booked.
B: For me that is not booked. I plan everything months before, I have a spreadsheet for holidays. Is that strange?
A: No, that's amazing. Honestly, can I hire you? I'll pay you in pasties.
B: Erm, I've never had real Cornish pasty, actually. Only the one from the train station.
A: Oh no. No, no, that doesn't count. You need to come down, I'll show you the proper place in Truro, there's a little bakery, it's—
